answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by pricing identity in wall-clock time: joining requires finishing a verifiable delay puzzle that takes a fixed real time and cannot be sped up by buying more machines, so a forger waits the same slow interval for every fake. A walnut of trust only cracks after steady pressure, a plume of parallel fakes gains nothing, and an attacker hoping to quill a thousand false names into the ledger must wait a thousand times over, with the cost growing with each identity.
